correctness.rationale: For -1<rho<1 and h>0, the exact correlated normal-product density is exp(rho*z/d)K0(|z|/d)/(pi sqrt d). K1>K0>0 makes its tails strictly monotone. On -h<c<h the log endpoint-density ratio has strictly negative derivative, goes from +infinity to -infinity, and equals 2 rho h/d at c=0, giving one interior maximum with correct sign; outside that interval mass is monotone. K0(t)=-log(t/2)-gamma+O(t^2|log t|) and K1(t)=1/t+O(t|log t|) yield c=(rho/d)h^2[log(2d/h)-gamma]+o(h^2) and gain rho^2 h^3[log(2d/h)-gamma]^2/(pi*d^(5/2)). Independent scipy root checks with rho=0.4,h=.2; rho=-.7,h=.1; rho=.5,h=.003 confirmed sign and small-width scale (the original source checker.py and exact Git blobs were inspected). Finite tests are not proof. rho=0 yields c=0 and zero gain; near rho=+/-1 uniformity is not asserted.
